--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [KaplanMeier]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | greenwood description: Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator of the survival function. twitter-card: title: >- [KaplanMeier]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | greenwood description: Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator of the survival function. title: "[KaplanMeier]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator of the survival function. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Kaplan-Meier product-limit estimator of the survival function. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_nonparametric.py#L341-L987){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature KaplanMeier( *, conf_type="log", conf_level=0.95, robust=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Kaplan-Meier estimator is a non-parametric method to estimate the survival function from right-censored data. It computes the survival probability at each observed event time as the product of conditional survival probabilities, accounting for subjects still at risk. This is the most widely used method for survival analysis and is the starting point for comparing survival between groups or assessing model fit. To use this estimator, call `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.fit()` with a right-censored response: an `Outcome` such as `gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status")` or a formula such as `"Surv(time, status) ~ sex"` together with `data=`, or a `Surv` built from values in hand. The estimator computes survival probabilities, standard errors, and confidence intervals at each unique event time. Results can be accessed as aligned arrays, exported to pandas/polars/pyarrow DataFrames, or queried through methods like `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.median()`, `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.quantile()`, and `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.predict()`. The implementation uses the product-limit formula $$ S(t) = \prod_{t_i \le t} \frac{n_i - d_i}{n_i} $$ where $n_i$ is the number at risk and $d_i$ is the number of events at time $t_i$. Variance uses Greenwood's formula, and confidence intervals can be constructed on the log, log-log, or identity scale. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [conf_type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["log"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence-interval transform: `"log"` (default, as in R's `survfit`), `"plain"`, or `"log-log"`. [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the interval (default 0.95). [robust]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Use the infinitesimal-jackknife (sandwich) variance instead of Greenwood's formula (the default is `False`). When `True`, standard errors and confidence intervals account for the correlation structure induced by weighted or correlated observations, matching R's `survfit(..., robust = TRUE)`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Fitted estimator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Call `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.fit()` to produce a fitted estimator with cached results (`time_`, `surv_`, `std_error_`, `conf_low_`, `conf_high_`, `n_risk_`, `n_event_`, `n_censor_`), accessible as aligned arrays or exported to DataFrames. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} Call `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.fit` with a `Surv` response. Results are exposed as aligned arrays (`time_`, `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.survival_`, `std_error_`, `conf_low_`, `conf_high_`, `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.strata_`), as tidy frames via `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.to_frame()` (optionally `format=`), and through `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.median`, `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.quantile`, and `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.predict`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Name the response columns of the bundled `lung` dataset with `gw.Outcome.surv()` and fit the estimator with `data=`. Printing the fitted object reports the median survival and its confidence interval. ::: {#e965f2a3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and name the response columns lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") # Fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) km ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` KaplanMeier (Kaplan-Meier survival estimate) n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL all 228 165 310 285 363 ``` ::: ::: The full step function, one row per event time, is available with `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.to_frame`. Pass `format=` to choose the backend (here, Polars): ::: {#7946523e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Export the survival curve as a Polars DataFrame km.to_frame(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

[fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator to survival data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_nonparametric.py#L451-L563){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature fit( surv, *, data=None, by=None, weights=None, cluster=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes the product-limit survival estimate from a `Surv` response (time-to-event data, possibly right-censored). The estimator remains in the fitted object after calling `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.fit()`. Access it via attributes like `surv`{.gd-no-link}, `time`, `n_risk`, etc., or access raw tables with `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.to_frame()` (optionally `format=`). Pass `by=` to produce separate curves per group (stratified analysis). Each group's fit is stored independently and can be visualized with `plot_survival()`. The fit is exact and no distributional assumptions are made. Optionally supply `weights=` (e.g., inverse-probability-of-censoring weights from the survey literature) to adjust for selection bias or survey design. Confidence intervals use the method specified at instantiation (`conf_type`), typically Greenwood's variance estimator. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `Surv` response (typically right-censored, but supports counting-process and other forms). Built with `Surv()`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side names the `by` column(s). [by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional grouping variable (e.g., a column or array). Produces one fit (one curve) per unique value of `by`, enabling stratified Kaplan-Meier analysis. Each group's results are stored and can be accessed separately via `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.to_frame()`, or visualized as separate curves via `plot_survival()`. Default (`None`) means to fit a single, unstratified curve. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional weights (e.g., from survey design or inverse-probability-of-censoring adjustments). Must have the same length as `surv`{.gd-no-link}. Default (`None`): unit weights. [cluster]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional cluster labels for grouped robust variance estimation. When provided, `robust=True` is implied. Per-subject influences are summed within each cluster before squaring, accounting for within-cluster correlation. Default (`None`) means no clustering. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response, `by`, `weights`, and `cluster`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KaplanMeier]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator object itself (for method chaining) with cached results (`time_`, `surv_`, `conf_low_`, `conf_high_`, `n_risk_`, `n_event_`, etc. as attributes). ::: #### Details {.doc-details} The Kaplan-Meier estimator is a non-parametric maximum likelihood estimator of the survival function $S(t)$. It is defined as the product of $(1 - d/n)$ over all event times up to $t$, where $d$ is the number of events and $n$ is the number at risk at each time. Confidence intervals are point-wise. They do not guarantee that the true curve lies entirely within the band. #### Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a single (unstratified) survival curve on the bundled `lung` dataset: ::: {#715ef8ab .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and name the response columns lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") # Fit a single unstratified survival curve km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) km ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` KaplanMeier (Kaplan-Meier survival estimate) n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL all 228 165 310 285 363 ``` ::: ::: Fit stratified curves by sex by passing `by="sex"`. This produces one curve per group, and the formula `"Surv(time, status) ~ sex"` gives the same fit. The results are stored and can be visualized separately: ::: {#f50dc8c8 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Fit stratified curves by sex and plot them km_stratified = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, by="sex", data=lung) gw.plot_survival(km_stratified) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### [median()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Median survival time, with confidence limits, for each curve. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_nonparametric.py#L672-L719){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature median( *, format=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The median survival time is the time at which the survival curve first drops to 0.5, when half of subjects have had the event. It is a key summary when comparing survival across groups. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per curve, with columns `strata`, `time`, `conf_low`, and `conf_high`. The layout is the same for one curve (`strata` is `"all"`) as for several. The median is `nan` when the curve never drops to 0.5. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} This is `~~greenwood.KaplanMeier.quantile()` at `p=0.5`, without the `prob` column. When the curve jumps over 0.5, the first time it reaches or falls below 0.5 is used. #### Examples {.doc-examples} The median survival time for each sex, with confidence limits: ::: {#3629b086 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit one curve per sex lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ sex", data=lung) # Median survival time with confidence limits km.median(format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

[what]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["survival"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"survival"` (default) for the survival probability $S(t)$, or `"cumhaz"` for the cumulative hazard $H(t)$. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per curve and time, with columns `strata`, `time`, and `estimate`. The layout is the same for one curve (`strata` is `"all"`) as for several. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} The curves are right-continuous step functions, so the value at time $t$ is the last step at a time $\le t$. Before the first step it is 1 for survival and 0 for the cumulative hazard. #### Examples {.doc-examples} Survival probabilities at 180, 365, and 730 days: ::: {#4ccefd4b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) # Read survival probabilities at specific time points km.predict(times=[180, 365, 730], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

For example, `p=0.25` gives the first-quartile time. Confidence limits come from inverting the pointwise confidence band, as R's `quantile.survfit()` does. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One or more proportions between 0 and 1. For example, `0.5` is the median, and `[0.25, 0.5, 0.75]` gives the three quartiles. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per curve and proportion, with columns `strata`, `prob`, `time`, `conf_low`, and `conf_high`. The layout is the same for one curve (`strata` is `"all"`) as for several. A quantile is `nan` when the curve (or a confidence limit) never drops to `1 - p`. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} The quantile is the smallest time $t$ with $S(t) \le 1 - p$. Its confidence limits are the same crossing times for the lower and upper confidence curves. These are pointwise, not simultaneous, intervals. #### Examples {.doc-examples} The three quartiles of survival time, with their confidence limits: ::: {#adc22e48 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) # Survival-time quartiles with confidence limits km.quantile(p=[0.25, 0.5, 0.75], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### [rmrl()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Restricted mean residual life at time `s`, over the window $(s, \tau]$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_nonparametric.py#L785-L855){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature rmrl( s, tau, *, format=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The expected additional survival time beyond a landmark `s`, for subjects who have survived to `s`, restricted to `tau`: $$ \mathrm{RMRL}(s; \tau) = \frac{\int_s^\tau S(u) \, du}{S(s)} $$ It generalizes the restricted mean survival time (which is `rmrl(0, tau)`) to a later landmark, for example the remaining life expectancy of patients who reached a milestone. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [s]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The landmark time. Must be non-negative. [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The end of the window. Must be greater than `s`. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per curve, with columns `strata`, `s`, `tau`, `estimate`, `std_error`, `conf_low`, and `conf_high`. The layout is the same for one curve (`strata` is `"all"`) as for several. The estimate is `nan` for a curve where everyone has had the event by `s`. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} The variance is the restricted-mean estimator applied to the conditional curve, summed over event times in $(s, \tau]$. The confidence limits are $\text{estimate} \pm z \cdot \text{se}$, with the lower limit floored at 0. #### Examples {.doc-examples} The expected additional survival time at 180 days, over the window out to 730 days: ::: {#e495fa6c .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) # Restricted mean residual life at 180 days km.rmrl(s=180, tau=730, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### [rmst()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Restricted mean survival time up to `tau` (the area under the survival curve). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_nonparametric.py#L721-L783){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature rmst( tau, *, format=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The restricted mean survival time is the expected survival time over the window $[0, \tau]$: the area under the survival curve up to `tau`. Unlike the median, it uses all the follow-up in the window, is defined even when the curve never reaches 0.5, and reads as an average (for example, mean survival over the first year). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The end of the window. Typically a clinically relevant horizon (for example, 1, 5, or 10 years). [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format: `None` (default), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. When `None`, a backend is auto-detected (Polars, then Pandas, then PyArrow). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pandas.DataFrame, polars.DataFrame, or pyarrow.Table]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One row per curve, with columns `strata`, `tau`, `estimate`, `std_error`, `conf_low`, and `conf_high`. The layout is the same for one curve (`strata` is `"all"`) as for several. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} $$ \mathrm{RMST}(\tau) = \int_0^\tau S(t) \, dt $$ is computed exactly from the step-function curve. The standard error is R's `survfit` restricted-mean estimator, and the confidence limits are $\text{estimate} \pm z \cdot \text{se}$, with the lower limit floored at 0. #### Examples {.doc-examples} The mean survival time over the first 365 days, with confidence limits: ::: {#41b1616d .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load data and fit the Kaplan-Meier estimator lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") km = gw.KaplanMeier().fit(death, data=lung) # Restricted mean survival time over 365 days km.rmst(tau=365, format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
